headline: Spanish 102 Foundation
threshold: Expand Spanish 101 through past narration, objects, plans, requests, commands and introductory subjunctive choices.

lessons.title: Past events in sequence
lessons.objective: Past events in sequence: Use the preterite for bounded events and connectors to order them; time words provide context.

words.es: Ayer llegué tarde a la estación.
words.en: Yesterday I arrived late at the station.
First I looked for the correct exit.
Then I bought a one-way ticket.

words.es: El tren salió a las ocho.
Llamé a Elena y expliqué el problema.
words.en: I called Elena and explained the problem.
In the end we took a bus.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a late arrival. Use the preterite for bounded events and connectors to order them; time words provide context. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Preterite spelling in yo
lessons.objective: Preterite spelling in yo: In yo preterite, -car → -qué, -gar → -gué and -zar → -cé preserve the sound; the other endings stay regular.

words.es: Busqué una mesa cerca de la ventana.
words.en: I looked for a table near the window.
I began to read the menu.

words.es: Almorcé con una amiga del trabajo.
words.en: I had lunch with a friend from work.
I paid the bill by card.

words.es: Saqué el recibo de mi bolso.
words.en: I took the receipt out of my bag.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing paying for lunch. In yo preterite, -car → -qué, -gar → -gué and -zar → -cé preserve the sound; the other endings stay regular. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Strong preterite stems
lessons.objective: Strong preterite stems: Tener → tuv-, estar → estuv-, poder → pud- and hacer → hic- use unaccented strong-preterite endings; hacer has hizo.

words.es: Tuve una cita en el centro.
El autobús estuvo lleno toda la mañana.
words.en: The bus was full all morning.
I could not get there on time.

words.es: La recepcionista puso mi nombre en otra lista.
words.en: The receptionist put my name on another list.

words.es: Hice una llamada desde la entrada.
words.en: I made a call from the entrance.

words.es: Al final el médico hizo espacio en su horario.
words.en: In the end the doctor made room in his schedule.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a difficult appointment. Tener → tuv-, estar → estuv-, poder → pud- and hacer → hic- use unaccented strong-preterite endings; hacer has hizo. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Third-person changes in -ir preterite
lessons.objective: Third-person changes in -ir preterite: Certain -ir verbs change e → i or o → u only in the third-person preterite: pidió, pidieron, durmió, durmieron.

words.es: Mi primo pidió una habitación tranquila.
words.en: My cousin asked for a quiet room.

words.es: La recepcionista repitió el número del piso.
words.en: The receptionist repeated the floor number.

words.es: Mi primo durmió hasta las nueve.
Sus hijos durmieron un poco más.
words.en: His children slept a little longer.

words.es: Por la mañana todos pidieron agua.
words.en: In the morning everyone asked for water.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing an overnight visit. Certain -ir verbs change e → i or o → u only in the third-person preterite: pidió, pidieron, durmió, durmieron. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Imperfect background
lessons.objective: Imperfect background: The imperfect describes background and ongoing conditions: -aba for -ar, -ía for -er/-ir.

words.en: We used to live near the river.

words.es: Nuestra casa tenía un patio pequeño.
words.en: Our house had a small courtyard.
My grandmother looked after the plants.

words.es: Yo iba a la escuela a pie.
words.en: I used to walk to school.

words.es: Desde la ventana veíamos las montañas.
words.en: From the window we could see the mountains.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing the old neighborhood. The imperfect describes background and ongoing conditions: -aba for -ar, -ía for -er/-ir. Ser, ir and ver are irregular. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Habit versus completed event
lessons.objective: Habit versus completed event: The imperfect frames habits and background; the preterite presents an event as bounded.

words.en: I normally used to have breakfast at home.

words.es: El lunes desayuné en la estación.
words.en: On Monday I had breakfast at the station.

words.es: Siempre llevaba un libro en la mochila.
words.en: I always used to carry a book in my backpack.
That day I forgot the backpack.

words.es: Mientras esperaba el tren, compré un periódico.
words.en: While I was waiting for the train, I bought a newspaper.

words.es: El viaje fue distinto de lo habitual.
words.en: The journey was different from the usual one.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a changed routine. The imperfect frames habits and background; the preterite presents an event as bounded. Both can describe the same situation from different viewpoints. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: An interrupted action
lessons.objective: An interrupted action: Use imperfect for an action in progress and preterite for the interrupting event: leía cuando sonó.

words.es: Leía un mensaje cuando sonó el teléfono.
words.en: I was reading a message when the phone rang.

words.es: Mi hermana estaba en la puerta.
words.en: My sister was at the door.

words.es: Buscaba mis llaves cuando ella llamó otra vez.
words.en: I was looking for my keys when she called again.

words.es: Abrí la puerta y le pedí un minuto.
words.en: I opened the door and asked her for a minute.

words.es: Mientras ella esperaba, encontré las llaves.
words.en: While she was waiting, I found the keys.
We left together for the station.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing the missing call. Use imperfect for an action in progress and preterite for the interrupting event: leía cuando sonó. Cuando alone does not dictate a tense. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Duration with desde and hace
lessons.objective: Duration with desde and hace: Desde names a starting point; desde hace names elapsed duration.

words.en: I have lived here since January.

words.es: Trabajo en la biblioteca desde hace dos meses.
words.en: I have worked at the library for two months.

words.es: Hace tres semanas conocí a mis vecinos.
words.en: I met my neighbors three weeks ago.

words.es: No veo a mi hermano desde el verano.
words.en: I have not seen my brother since the summer.
How long have you been studying Spanish?

words.es: Estudio español desde el año pasado.
words.en: I have been studying Spanish since last year.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a new resident. Desde names a starting point; desde hace names elapsed duration. With an ongoing situation, Spanish often uses present where English uses have been. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Direct objects in context
lessons.objective: Direct objects in context: Lo, la, los and las replace a direct object and agree with its grammatical gender and number.

words.en: Do you have the hotel reservation?

words.es: Sí, la tengo en el teléfono.
words.en: Yes, I have it on my phone.
Where did you put the tickets?

words.es: Los puse dentro de la mochila.
words.en: I put them inside the backpack.

words.es: Necesito el pasaporte, pero no lo encuentro.
words.en: I need the passport, but I cannot find it.

words.es: Aquí está; lo dejaste sobre la mesa.
words.en: Here it is; you left it on the table.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing packing a bag. Lo, la, los and las replace a direct object and agree with its grammatical gender and number. Put them before a conjugated verb. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Indirect objects and recipients
lessons.objective: Indirect objects and recipients: Me, te, le, nos and les identify the recipient or person affected.

words.es: Le escribí a Rosa esta mañana.
words.en: I wrote to Rosa this morning.

words.es: Le expliqué el cambio de horario.
words.en: I explained the schedule change to her.

words.es: Nos mandó la dirección del nuevo local.
words.en: She sent us the address of the new venue.
Did you let the others know?

words.es: Sí, les envié un mensaje a todos.
words.en: Yes, I sent a message to all of them.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing sending a message. Me, te, le, nos and les identify the recipient or person affected. A named recipient can clarify le or les: le escribí a Rosa. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.
